items.question: Vincristine, an anticancer drug, acts by?

*PharmaCraft Daily - 22 Nov 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Anticancer & Immuno)
Q: Vincristine, an anticancer drug, acts by?
Ans: Inhibiting microtubule assembly
Why: Vincristine binds tubulin and prevents microtubule assembly, arresting mitosis; causes neuropathy.

🌍 *FMGE* (Anticancer & Immuno)
Q: Cyclophosphamide can cause haemorrhagic cystitis, prevented by?
Ans: Hydration and mesna
Why: Mesna binds the toxic metabolite acrolein in the bladder, with hydration, preventing haemorrhagic cystitis.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Anticancer & Immuno)
Q: Bevacizumab inhibits angiogenesis by targeting?
Ans: VEGF
Why: Bevacizumab binds VEGF, inhibiting tumour angiogenesis; risks bleeding, hypertension, impaired healing.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Anticancer & Immuno)
Q: Why does rasburicase help prevent tumour lysis nephropathy better than allopurinol?
Ans: It enzymatically degrades existing uric acid to allantoin
Why: Rasburicase (urate oxidase) breaks down existing uric acid, unlike allopurinol which only blocks formation.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper I: General/Experimental)
Q: The dose ratio in a Schild analysis is used to calculate the antagonist's?
Ans: pA2/affinity (pKB)
Why: The Schild plot of log(dose ratio-1) versus log[antagonist] yields the antagonist dissociation constant (pA2/pKB).
